# SPE round r01: build and evaluate the triage agent

Your prompt is the spec: "triage tickets correctly and cheaply." This plan is the r01 prediction. The eval is one Workflow run after you approve it.

Nothing exists yet. This round has to create the agent, a labeled ticket set, a grader, and the harness. Your prompt does not say what "correctly" or "cheaply" mean in numbers. I picked defaults for those and logged each one as an open decision for you below. If you approve the plan as written, the defaults apply.

I will commit locally after each step. I will not push. Commit messages will carry no Claude attribution lines.

## Decisions I need from you (defaults apply on approval)

| ID | Question | Default I chose |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | What tickets, and which categories? | Generic SaaS support tickets in 7 categories: `billing`, `bug`, `account_access`, `outage`, `feature_request`, `how_to`, `spam_other` |
| D2 | What does "correctly" mean for category? | Category accuracy of at least 90% on the held-out test set |
| D3 | Does triage include priority? | Yes. Priority runs P1 to P4. Priority accuracy must be at least 80%. P1 recall must be at least 95%, because a missed urgent ticket is the costliest error |
| D4 | What does "cheaply" mean? | Mean API cost of at most $0.002 per ticket |
| D5 | Where do tickets come from? | 150 synthetic tickets, because no real ones exist in the repo. Real tickets from you would be better for r02 |
| D6 | Which model provider? | The Anthropic API. I will read current model IDs and prices from the docs on build day and save them with the source URL and date |
| D7 | What runtime? | Node.js, so the agent, grader, and Workflow script share one language |

These rows go into `spe/spec/disagreements.md` with you as owner.

## Specify

I will save your prompt and any planning answers verbatim in `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md`.

`spe/spec/spec.md`, round r01:

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The agent returns exactly one category from the D1 set for each ticket | User: "triage tickets", D1 | G2 `category_exact`, a code check against the gold labels |
| R2 | The agent returns exactly one priority from P1 to P4 | D3 | G3 `priority_exact`, a code check |
| R3 | Category accuracy is at least 90% on the test set | User: "correctly", D2 | G2 |
| R4 | Priority accuracy is at least 80%, and P1 recall is at least 95% | User: "correctly", D3 | G3 and G4 `p1_recall` |
| R5 | Mean cost is at most $0.002 per ticket | User: "cheaply", D4 | G5 `cost_from_usage`, which computes cost from the token counts the API returns and the saved price table |
| R6 | 100% of outputs parse against `triage/schema.json` | Decision: the output feeds other systems | G1 `schema_valid` |

Rejected for r01: latency targets and routing to named teams. You did not ask for them. Both are logged in `disagreements.md` as possible r02 rows.

All six checks are code. No LLM judge is needed this round.

## Predict

Configurations (each one changes one thing from A):

- **K**: keyword rules with no model. This is the floor.
- **A**: the current Haiku model, zero-shot, with category and priority definitions in the prompt.
- **B**: A plus 8 few-shot examples taken from the dev set.
- **C**: A with the current Sonnet model swapped in.

| Metric | K | A | B | C | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy (%) | 55 | 84 | 89 | 91 | G2 | The hard 30% of tickets need context that keywords miss. Few-shot and a larger model each recover part of that 30% |
| Priority accuracy (%) | 45 | 70 | 76 | 79 | G3 | Priority depends on business impact, and tone misleads models. Angry low-impact tickets will get rated too high |
| P1 recall (%) | 60 | 85 | 90 | 93 | G4 | Calm reports of outages are the main way a model misses P1 tickets |
| Schema valid (%) | 100 | 98 | 99 | 100 | G1 | Small models sometimes add prose around the JSON. Few-shot examples show the exact output shape |
| Mean cost per ticket (USD) | 0.0000 | 0.0012 | 0.0027 | 0.0035 | G5 | About 850 input and 60 output tokens per ticket. Few-shot adds about 1,500 input tokens. Estimate only, at list prices I will confirm on build day |
| Requirements met (count of 6) | 2 | 3 | 4 | 4 | G1 to G5 | K fails on accuracy. A fails on accuracy. B and C fail on cost |
| Meets all requirements (1 = yes) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | G1 to G5 | No config passes everything in r01. Accuracy and cost pull in opposite directions without prompt caching or a better prompt |

Naive guess for the prediction log: every model config scores 85% category, 75% priority, and 85% P1 recall. I will report plainly if this flat guess beats my numbers.

`same_as_last_round` is false for every number, because r01 is the first round.

## Evaluate

### Build steps (before the Workflow)

1. **Agent.** I will create `triage/agent.js`, `triage/prompt.md`, `triage/categories.yaml`, and `triage/schema.json`. The agent takes ticket text and a config name. It returns `{category, priority, reason}` and records token usage.
2. **Ticket set.** I will write the label first and then the ticket, so the gold label is the intent behind each ticket. The set has 150 tickets: 30 dev and 120 test. About 30% are hard cases: multi-issue tickets, angry tone with low impact, calm tone with an outage, sarcasm, non-English text, and spam that looks like billing. A separate Opus subagent reviews each label and flags any ambiguity. I will drop or relabel each flagged ticket and log the change.
   - `spe/evals/data/tickets-dev.jsonl`
   - `spe/evals/data/tickets-test.jsonl` (ticket text only, no labels)
   - `spe/evals/gold/test-labels.jsonl` (the answer key, which the agent never reads)
3. **Grader.** `spe/evals/harness/grade.js` runs checks G1 to G5. `spe/evals/harness/prices.yaml` holds the prices with the source URL and date.
4. **Workflow script.** `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` holds `const ROUND = "r01"`. All prompt text and paths use that constant.

Subagents in the harness (the label reviewer, failure analysis, and the critic) run on Opus. The Haiku and Sonnet models appear only as the agent under test in configs A to C.

### Workflow steps and gates

1. **Gate: grader selftest.** Gold labels fed back as answers must score 100%. Empty output must fail G1. Wrong labels (shifted by one category) must score under 20%. The run halts on any failure.
2. **Gate: control.** No prior round exists to regrade. Instead I will grade config K twice. The two scores must match exactly.
3. **Gate: dry run.** The dry run covers 3 cells: A on ticket 1, B on ticket 2, and C on ticket 3. Each cell must pass G1 and log its usage. Its request payload must contain no gold label text.
4. **Full run.** Each model config runs the 120 test tickets 3 times, which is 1,080 calls. K runs once. A budget meter skips any trial that would cross the cap and logs the skip to `spe/evals/results/r01/skips.jsonl`.
5. **Leak scan.** The scan checks every request payload against the gold file and the predictions file. Any trial with a match is voided and logged.
6. **Split cells.** A cell is one config on one ticket. If its 3 runs disagree, it gets up to 2 more runs, for a cap of 5.
7. **Grade.** Scores go to `spe/evals/results/r01/scores.json`, with one value for each prediction cell.
8. **Failure analysis.** An Opus subagent groups wrong answers into candidate F-numbered failure types and cites ticket IDs for each one.
9. **Completeness critic.** An Opus subagent confirms that every prediction cell has a measured value and that every skip and void is logged. It also confirms that no trial read the grader, the gold file, or the predictions.

### Workflow arguments

```json
{
  "round": "r01",
  "configs": ["K", "A", "B", "C"],
  "test_set": "spe/evals/data/tickets-test.jsonl",
  "gold": "spe/evals/gold/test-labels.jsonl",
  "runs_per_cell": 3,
  "split_extra_cap": 2,
  "budget_usd": 10,
  "max_api_calls": 2000,
  "dry_run_cells": [["A", 1], ["B", 2], ["C", 3]]
}
```

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

- Trial API calls: about $0.43 for A, $0.97 for B, and $1.26 for C, which is about $2.70 in total. Split-cell reruns could add up to $1.
- Ticket generation and label review on Opus: about $1 to $3 in tokens, which is a rough guess.
- Workflow subagent tokens for analysis and the critic: I cannot measure these ahead of the run.
- The hard cap is $10 of API spend. The key is read from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Before the first paid call, I will confirm that pwd, the git remote, and the API account match this repo.

## Order of work and commits

1. **After approval, before anything else:** I will copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`. I will then write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. The file starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It holds the round, the date 2026-10-21, the author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", the configs, every number above with its Why, and `same_as_last_round: false`.
2. I will write the transcript, `spe.md`, and `disagreements.md`. Commit: `SPE r01 specify: triage spec with defaults D1 to D7`.
3. Commit the plan and prediction: `SPE r01 predict: no config meets all six requirements`.
4. I will build the agent and the ticket set. Commit: `SPE r01 evaluate (harness): triage agent v0 and ticket set`.
5. I will build the grader, the selftest, and the Workflow script. Commit: `SPE r01 evaluate (harness): grader, gates, workflow`.
6. I will launch the Workflow. When the completion notice arrives, I will commit the results: `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
7. **Close-out.** `spe/prediction-log.md` gets one row per cell with the Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer columns. A "Which Why broke" section quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption. `spe/failures.md` records each new F-type with the fields Name, Kind, Round, What, How to spot it, Seen in, and Fix. The spec gets a "Proposed for round r02" table. I will write `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft` and update `spe/README.md`. Commit: `SPE r01 learn: <headline>`, and tag `spe-r01`.

The saved r01 prediction will not change after any trial runs. If I find a grader bug after the run, I will log it as a failure and show the original and regraded numbers side by side.

## Halt conditions

I will stop and report to you if:

- the budget cap is hit
- an answer key leaks into a trial
- the grader selftest or the control fails
- a result depends on D1 to D7 in a way only you can settle

If every config passes everything, r02 needs harder tickets or stricter graders. The loop can stop only after 3 rounds in a row where predictions match results, so r01 cannot be the last round.
